source_text:
# A STRESS DOMAIN, NOT AN EXAMPLE — lives under qa/stress_domains/, not
# examples/, on purpose (see qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook's own
# "being clever" note and .claude/skills/qa-loop/SKILL.md's Phase 4).
#
# TARGETED AT ONE SPECIFIC, ALREADY-CONFIRMED DIVERGENCE CLASS: an entity
# command dispatched with BOTH a nonexistent addressed element AND an
# argument that fails its own invariant. ADR 0037's re-verification
# (2026-09-09) found Ruby and Rust disagree on which refusal wins for
# exactly this shape on `Banking::Account.LedgerEntry.Amend` (seed 34) —
# Ruby raises the argument's InvariantViolation first, Rust answers
# NotFound because its entity-addressing extraction never builds/
# invariant-checks a typed value object for the addressing field at all.
# Confirmed still open, correctly left unfixed (needs a real codegen
# capability, not a one-line guard) — this domain is the re-trigger-in-
# a-new-context half of the loop's own strategy: same class of bug,
# unrelated business shape, to see whether it's LedgerEntry-specific or
# general to every entity command.
Hecks.bluebook "LedgerOrdering" do
  vision "One aggregate, one entity, one command that takes an invariant-checked argument while addressing the entity by id — deliberately minimal, built to answer one question: does Ruby and Rust's argument-invariant-vs-entity-existence ordering disagreement generalize past LedgerEntry.Amend?"

  core

  aggregate "Folder" do
    description "A folder holding slips, addressed by reference."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference, FolderReference
    attribute :slips,     list_of(Slip)

    value_object "FolderReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a folder is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Start a folder"

      attribute :reference, FolderReference

      emits "FolderOpened"
    end

    command "AddSlip" do
      role "Clerk"
      goal "Add a slip to the folder"

      reference_to Folder
      attribute :reference, SlipReference
      attribute :amount,    SlipAmount

      sets :slips, append: { reference: :reference, amount: :amount }

      emits "SlipAdded"
    end

    value_object "SlipReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a slip is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # THE INVARIANT AT THE CENTER OF THE STRESS TEST — positive only, so
    # `amount.value=-1` is guaranteed to fail it, and a nonexistent
    # `to.entity` is guaranteed to fail existence. Same dispatch, both
    # failures true at once: which one the runtime reports first is
    # exactly what's under test.
    value_object "SlipAmount" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a slip amount is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    entity "Slip" do
      description "One slip in the folder, with an amount that must be positive."

      identified_by :reference

      attribute :reference, SlipReference
      attribute :amount,    SlipAmount, optional: true

      # THE STRESS COMMAND. Dispatch this against a `to.entity` that does
      # not exist, carrying an `amount.value` that fails its own
      # invariant, on BOTH engines, and diff which refusal comes back.
      command "Amend" do
        role "Clerk"
        goal "Change what a slip is worth"

        attribute :amount, SlipAmount

        sets :amount

        emits "SlipAmended"
      end
    end
  end
end
